attempted_claim: Let G be the discrete graph obtained by gluing two 3-mandarin graphs serially (Band–Lévy Proposition 5.8 with n=3, M=2, S=0). Consider compact metric quantum graphs Gamma(G;l) with standard (Neumann–Kirchhoff) vertex conditions and total length normalized to 1, over the closed length simplex closure(L_G) allowing zero lengths (edge contractions). Determine S(G)=sup_l k_1[Gamma(G;l)] where k_1=sqrt(lambda_1) is the first positive wavenumber; determine whether the supremum is attained at strictly positive lengths (maximizer) or only on the boundary (proper supremizer with contracted topology); and decide whether any supremizer is a stower graph or a mandarin graph in the sense of Band–Lévy Section 9 — in particular, with the explicit competing values that the symmetric mandarin-chain critical point has simple gap k_1=3*pi while the contracted equilateral 4-petal flower/stower gives k_1=4*pi: is the supremizer a stower/mandarin with the Section 9 predicted value, or does G admit an exotic supremizer outside these two families?
decisive_failure: No rigorous global upper bound S(G)<=4pi over the closed length 5-simplex was established: the disjoint two-arch variational route failed on support-disjointness at the middle vertex, the closure-stratification route was not completed, and the numerical simplex scans are evidence only. The secular solver and scan scripts are preserved as verification-critical artifacts but do not constitute a proof of the supremum or the stower/mandarin-versus-exotic classification.
